A really enjoyable game to play seriously or for the jankiness, accurate to the science behind it, plenty of well made graphics overhaul and utility mods to sink hundreds of hours.

The learning curve is steep for doing crazier stuff or building good rockets/planes, which is part of the process to practice applied engineering (problem solving). In case of skill issue, there's great content from people like Scott Manley, Matt Lowne, Stratzenblitz75 to get inspiration from, or see how's it properly done. Maybe you can fish some life inspiration there too!

Forcing complaints, I don't like the price of the DLCs for what they add, mods do better, and I just wished we had steam achievements to track progress and reasons to do harder stuff!

Just amazing. This game can cater for those who like to fool around, right to the very top of the ladder with absolute expert Scott Manly's out there. Challenge yourself. Blow shit up. Build a space station. Build a tank. Finely tune a hyper-manuverable jet. Make a plane out of nothing but fuel and engines to burn it.
This game is so versatile, you could literally get anyone to play it.

I have worked in the space industry since the 1990's and have/am doing GNC and orbit dynamics on occasion. Many of my colleagues in the industry have played or continue to play this game which is how I came to play it.

It is crazy how good this games is at portraying physics. I am still astounded at how quickly it can get concepts across. It would have been so awesome if game like this was available when I was in school, but no... I was stuck with having professors writing equations on the board and poor explanations.

For those of you going to school now learning about orbit dynamics and space engineering - I envy you to have things like this to learn from. Goodness knows how much better KSP-2 will be.

Okay lads, I figured out how to disable the launcher in the newest version.
Grab the file path to "KSP_64.exe" located in your install directory, and place it between the quotes with this formatting:
"FILE_PATH" %command%

Example:
"C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Kerbal Space Program\KSP_x64.exe" %command%

So im going to give you a short list of the pro's and cons and it will inevitably leave you with a sense of dread if this game is not already in your steam library (Shame on you!)

Endless Fun

Pros:
If you ever wonder how it feels to put a rocket up in orbit, to land on the moon or go to Mars, this the game for you.
That being said, it's as hard as you'd imagine and if you're no good at math then even worst. But there's something quite fascinating about putting together a trial and error rocket and landing it on the Mun for the first time.
There are different game modes which help you get better and understand the mechanics though, so it all works out in the end.

Cons:
Docking ships together is super hard but there are mods that help with that.
Sometimes it's a little glitchy, and finicky, but over all not bad at all.

Kebral Space Program is a fantastic game for people who enjoy Simulation and Exploration Games. KSP is a game where the players create and manage their own space program. Build spacecraft, fly them, and try to help the Kerbals fulfill their ultimate mission of conquering space.
The game handles a Vast Solar System containing a multitude of planets and moons. The biggest problem with the game is the poor optimization of certain aspects like time warps and the high quantity of objects in space.
Although the game is great and very fun to play, I do not recommend buying it as of 2022 as KSP2 will shortly be released.

KSP2: https://store.steampowered.com/app/954850/Kerbal_Space_Program_2/

This game is one of my favorites. I would buy if you enjoy the following:
- Enjoy space, and space exploration
- Like creating, building space worthy ships
- Do not get easily frustrated (TON of trial and error situations)
- Would like to understand the basics and even some advanced concepts of space flight
- Have a decent imagination and creativity (sky is almost the limit)
- Enjoy the gratification from reaching milestones (going further and further (and back) from your home planet)
- Do not mind few bugs
This game is not easy at all and it gets more difficult the further you progress. The good thing is that once you learn a certain concept you will feel comfortable and will be ready for next challenge. My favorite is the career mode! :) You get to start nice and easy with only few basic parts and as you progress you get more and more parts to build.

Jeb's need to go to space. And you need to built him a rocket, or 2 or 3 or..... You want him to explore the Mun (moon) and other parts of space. The models are quite fun to watch (and explode). After crashing Jeb for the 10th time, you start to think in fact, that this is a pretty hard and difficult game. And it is! The fun in this game, let's you tackle NASA-tasks in a blink of an eye and still have a good laugh.

Go plant that flag on anyone of these planets!

This is the most awesome game I've ever played. If you get into one game in your life, let it be this!

It takes a bit to get into everything but it's as much fun when you have no idea what you're doing as it is when you do.

With the "Breaking Ground" DLC you can even generate science points by crashing things in the ground.

After playing this, every other game feels somewhat limited.
Even "open world" stuff suddenly clearly has its limits.

And if you get tired of everything being 1/10th the "real" size, you can install a huge nuber of mods, some of which can scale up things so it feels more realistic.

reason.text: Negative reviews from this period mostly object to a new EULA that they call spyware, citing privacy concerns and Red Shell analytics software.
A news report from June 2018 covers Red Shell analytics software and privacy concerns, the same topic these reviews raise.

lines.F1: Kerbal Space Program had a negative surge (far more negative reviews than usual, often called a review bomb), May 2018 to Jun 2018
lines.F2: May 2018: 39% positive across 721 reviews (439 negative), against a usual 89% positive and 36 negative a month
lines.F3: Jun 2018: 49% positive across 620 reviews (314 negative), against a usual 81% positive and 95 negative a month

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (96%): players praise the mods and customization.
The most common complaint is bugs and crashes.

details.text: Recent reviews complain about bugs and crashes far less than older ones, and the overall score has held close to its all-time level.
Players in their first hours are far less positive than long-time players, at 74% against 97%.
